pr_title: Implement a cooldown period for config entry reloads
pr_body:
## Breaking change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Config entry reloads now implement a 30s cooldown to prevent multiple successive reloads.  If multiple reloads are requested, the first one will happen immediately. Subsequent reload requests will be grouped and happen 30s after the last reload.

The EntityRegistryDisabledHandler now relies on this logic instead of implementing its own similar logic.

## Proposed change

#73387 #73145 #72636 fixed cases where the config entry could have been reloaded concurrently or before it was ever finished loading, and generally solved the issues where the setup and data being fetched to support the integration could get in a bad state.

However, the previous fixes did not address the case that entities may get added again or be in an unexpected state since forwarded platform setups happen in tasks via `async_add_entities` that we do not wait to be complete before declaring the reload complete when they happen after Home Assistant starts.

I expect this will fix at least some of these [classes](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+sort%3Aupdated-desc+%22does+not+generate+unique+IDs%22) of previously unexplained bugs.

pr_comments: This does fix the issue, but I'm not sure I like the implementation
I think I'm going to start over with this one as I think I want to use the Debouncer instead and move the reload function to the entry itself
I can't do that because we would then have to teach the entry about when a reload is allowed

We really can't wait 30s for the 2nd reload with the current design as everything stalls

Will have to think about that case. It likely just has to happen in the background in that case.  Ideally we could give feedback though but that may not be realistic since the action is so far away from the cause at this point that it may not be useful anyways
Would it not be simpler to skip the second reload and just have a check to see if reload is currently happening and thereby not starting a second one (even with delay)?

> Would it not be simpler to skip the second reload and just have a check to see if reload is currently happening and thereby not starting a second one (even with delay)?

I wish we could but we don't know at what point in the process the first reload is at so if an option changes in the middle of the reload we have no idea if it loaded up with the old option or the new one so we have to do another reload to make sure the change is effective 

Edit: For clarity the platforms could be using the stale data but we know the init function has the good data since that happens under the lock but even then it would have the data from the first reload request since we don't lock the data

> > Would it not be simpler to skip the second reload and just have a check to see if reload is currently happening and thereby not starting a second one (even with delay)?
> 
> I wish we could but we don't know at what point in the process the first reload is at so if an option changes in the middle of the reload we have no idea if it loaded up with the old option or the new one so we have to do another reload to make sure the change is effective 
> 
> Edit: For clarity the platforms could be using the stale data but we know the init function has the good data since that happens under the lock but even then it would have the data from the first reload request since we don't lock the data

Probably to complex for this but it sounds it would be more logical to block a config entry change during load/unload/reload since a user could in theory "bomb it" with requests.

> Probably to complex for this but it sounds it would be more logical to block a config entry change during load/unload/reload since a user could in theory "bomb it" with requests.

We don't know when its actually done since the config entry creates background tasks to setup the entities which are untracked by the config entry

Everything seems to work quite well.

This is going to break a lot of tests though as they assume reloads are atomic and they definitely are not

All the test failures are actual failure cases that this change is designed to prevent.

The tests are actually relying on being able to reload multiple times in quick succession, which works fine if you don't ever assert that the platforms loaded correctly

Some of these failures are because the integration does a migration or sets the unique id and reloads itself in the middle of the test, and then it proceeds do something else that triggers a reload which then gets ratelimited.

We are going to have to fix all of those before this can move forward 😢
Thankfully most of these are either bugs in the tests or won't actually happen in production but some of them actually could which would cause the problem this PR is solving
The ones that are still failing look like legitimate issues with the test (or the integration).  Each one will need to be fixed.
We should probably have a test reload helper like async_fire_time_changed since we don't want to import a constant
Almost got them all. Pushing between flight connections
Hopefully I can finish this up on the next flight.  Last one before back in TX
I think the plex test will still fail since it relies on both the reload and the time changing, but it just happens to use the time for the cooldown
The plex tests are relying on reloads not happening so they are going to be a bit harder to fix
If this implementation looks good I'll write a blog post as well
Pretty sure this will fix https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/73654 as well

> Pretty sure this will fix #73654 as well

Yes, I think so too. Thanks!

> previous fixes did not address the case that entities may get added again or be in an unexpected state since forwarded platform setups happen in tasks that we do not wait to be complete before declaring the reload complete

I think we should try to fix that instead of adding a 30s cooldown.

> > previous fixes did not address the case that entities may get added again or be in an unexpected state since forwarded platform setups happen in tasks that we do not wait to be complete before declaring the reload complete
> 
> I think we should try to fix that instead of adding a 30s cooldown.

Alternate PR https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/73806
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/73806 won't solve this problem since the entities are also created in tasks via `async_add_entities` which are not awaited, but its still good to do

`async_add_entities` happening in a task is also the same reason we didn't move https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/68488 forward.  Even with awaiting the platform forwards in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/73806 there is no deterministic way to know when a config entry is done creating entities following a reload which effectively makes the race period forever.  Practically speaking 30s seems like a good cutoff.

Marked as draft as its looking like may be possible to replace this PR with a combination of

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/73806
and
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/73828
Closing this PR, as it has been replaced by the above mentioned PRs

issue_context.title: Hue problem - "Platform hue does not generate unique IDs
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Sporadically, and out of nowhere, my Hue Integration (1 bridge, 2 hue lights) throws the error code and renders control of Hue devices inoperable.

It then ignores the hue intergration lights and entities, and then the log fills up with unable to communicate with bridge and lights.

A restart of HA fixes the issue, however, it has happened twice already.

The problem seems to orignally start with the issue of unique IDs, then the connection problems come after that. Why is it complianing about unque IDs?

Also, when looking the integration entities, there are a couple of entries that are added (circuled in red) and the onces circled in green the actual lights (2 of them)

![Hue](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/79593761/174350777-7bc4fc5b-9ced-4fc1-85fa-fb93ecebf6a3.png)



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

 2022.6.6

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

Hue

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/hue

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
below is a sample of the first sets of errors, 


Logger: homeassistant.components.light

Source: helpers/entity_platform.py:598
Integration: Light (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 2:20:24 AM (3 occurrences)
Last logged: 2:20:24 AM

Platform hue does not generate unique IDs. ID 9ed99fb4-912d-4fbd-a4a8-4d844a963abd already exists - ignoring light.hue_go_1
Platform hue does not generate unique IDs. ID a7e6ca74-3fc8-42c8-a569-5dd4bc85441c already exists - ignoring light.hue_lightstrip_plus_1
Platform hue does not generate unique IDs. ID 23b2d65b-135c-4dce-8111-8c350b41d3a8 already exists - ignoring light.basement_family_room
```


### Additional information

_No response_

Hey there @balloob, @marcelveldt, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`hue`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L466) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
Glad you're on the case! Cheers

Hi @bdraco, I wanted to provide some more information as this is happening to more more than I would like. A few days ago, i removed the Hue integration from HA and added it back (this time without the rooms from the Hue app, just the three devices, 1 bridge and 2 lights in HA).

 I had another instance of this happening again, here are the logs in question, in chronological order:

```
Logger: homeassistant.components.light
Source: helpers/entity_platform.py:598
Integration: Light (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 8:10:23 PM (2 occurrences)
Last logged: 8:10:23 PM

Platform hue does not generate unique IDs. ID 9ed99fb4-912d-4fbd-a4a8-4d844a963abd already exists - ignoring light.go_teams_status_night_light
Platform hue does not generate unique IDs. ID a7e6ca74-3fc8-42c8-a569-5dd4bc85441c already exists - ignoring light.lightstrip_projector_screen
```

and then

```
Logger: aiohue.v2[192.168.1.67].events
Source: /usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/aiohue/v2/controllers/events.py:239
First occurred: 8:12:33 PM (7 occurrences)
Last logged: 9:31:45 PM

30 Attempts to (re)connect to bridge failed - This might be an indication of connection issues.
40 Attempts to (re)connect to bridge failed - This might be an indication of connection issues.
50 Attempts to (re)connect to bridge failed - This might be an indication of connection issues.
60 Attempts to (re)connect to bridge failed - This might be an indication of connection issues.
70 Attempts to (re)connect to bridge failed - This might be an indication of connection issues.
```

The Hue intergration at this point, become broken, I couldn't control my Hue devices.

However, I noticed the IP address in the error logger above, 192.168.1.67, wasn't actually the same IP address of the Hue Bridge as reported by the Hue App. At this point, I realized its probably, somehow, my Hue bridge or router is changing the IP address of the bridge. 

What I've done now is I reserved the current IP and MAC address of the Hue bridge in my routers settings so it doesn't change it anymore.

I don't know if this is the problem or even it will be solved by reserving the IP/MAC address of the Hue bridge in my router...time will tell in the next few days.

I came here because my Hue integration started acting up in a similar (but different) way:
The status of my Hue lights is correctly reflected in Home Assistant, but I can't make changes (so turning off a light from HA, the light will stay on and after a few seconds the light again shows as on in HA -- if I turn it off from the Hue app it will turn off and the status in HA will update to off as well).

Similar to the previous post, I found connection errors in my logs and the IP address it's trying to connect to doesn't match what I can see in the Hue app:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/242196/176455063-69a3bdac-ae11-478e-92a4-d27a52a94f55.png)


In my case, the connection errors started before the unique ID errors:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/242196/176455647-6fb07ace-11cc-445f-af39-aa9dbc03c06d.png)

I tried reloading the Hue integration, although that didn't seem to change anything. Restarting HA did appear to (at least for now) resolve things.

Its been a week now that I have reserved the IP and MAC adddress of the Hue Bridge in my router, and the problems seems to have gone away. I don't know why the IP addrress was changing in the first place (could be my router or ISP).

Indeed restarting was a temporary fix for me, it would work, but then have the same problem 2 days later.

Perhaps the problem here is how the Hue integration deals with IP changes in a session?

If it happens again to you, try reserving the IP/MAC address in your router. Shoudl solve the issue.
The Hue integration should automatically update the Hue config entry and reload it when we detect the Hue hub broadcasting a new IP address via either SSDP or mDNS.

thanks @balloob ...its actually you, the father of HA!

With regards to the automatic config update, it doesn't seem to be updating because the Hue app is reporting another IP than what the logger is saying in the errord...so, im not certain what is happening here.

just wanted to provide an update to this. It seems there is a problem with my router/ISP in that the router reboots itself one or twice a day (still investigating the cause). In the process of doing this, it reassigns IP address to the connected devices once it comes back online. However, ever since I reserved the IP address of the Hue in the router settings, the error does not happen anymore (despite my router still restarting once a day on its own).

The changing IP  address, although caused by my router, may be causing the issue here for Hue.

Once we merge https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/73806 it should better handle the frequently changing ip case as it will eliminate the race.

Now that 2022.7 is wrapped, I'll try to finish that up
